Job Description:
What this job can offer you
Remote's SRE team exists so that our engineers can move quickly and our customers get a product that stays up. The team owns Kubernetes, AWS, PostgreSQL, CI infrastructure, our observability stack and the reliability practices that sits on top of all of it.
We are looking for a Team Leader to run that team. This is a 60% IC, 40% leadership role. You will own the career development of your reports, steer the teams focus using judgment against the company goals, and you will be the spokesperson for the team across engineering. You will also stay close enough to the technical work to set direction with credibility and to know when something is going wrong before it is escalated to you.
Reliability practice at Remote is maturing rather than mature. Our SLO framework is live on its first few teams and needs to reach the rest, there is real work to do on how we balance operational load against project delivery. If you want a team where the foundations are in place and the interesting problems are still open, this is that team.
What you bring
People leadership
You have led an SRE, infrastructure or platform engineering team, and you have owned your reports' growth, performance and career progression rather than just their sprints.
You coach both craft and the soft skills, you can point to people who grew because of it.
You handle underperformance directly and early, with clarity and empathy.
You have hired engineers, and you can tell the difference between a good interview and a good engineer.
You read team dynamics well and you resolve conflict rather than routing around it.
You have a natural talent fostering commitment to the goals of the company.
Technical depth
A hands-on background in site reliability, DevOps or cloud infrastructure engineering, deep enough that you can review your team's work, challenge a design and be taken seriously in an incident.
Kubernetes in production, including the operational reality of it rather than the happy path.
AWS at meaningful scale.
Hands on AI building, enablement, scaling AI infrastructure.
Solid o11y practices and principles,
Infrastructure as code with Terraform.
CI/CD systems such as GitLab CI, GitHub Actions or Jenkins.
Docker and shell scripting.
You have run a reliability practice: incident response, on-call, SLOs and error budgets, and the discipline of turning incidents into changes that stick.
Understanding and history of working in regulated environments.
Ways of working
You prioritise exceptionally well when operational load and project work compete, and you protect your team's focus without dropping the operational commitment.
You write clearly. Remote is fully distributed and async, so most of your leadership will happen in writing.
You build relationships across teams. A lot of SRE's value comes from being the team others bring problems to early.
Nice to have
Working knowledge of a backend language, ideally Elixir, or otherwise Java, Clojure, Node.js, Python or similar.
Depth in modern observability: OpenTelemetry, distributed tracing, and tools such as Honeycomb.
Database operations experience, particularly PostgreSQL or Aurora performance, connection pool health and query tuning.
Running and configuring Linux systems outside a cloud environment.
Security capability from both a defensive and an offensive standpoint.
Cloud cost management and FinOps.
Experience growing a team from a small base, including building the hiring bar as you go.
Key Responsibilities
Your people
The full career lifecycle of your reports: onboarding, feedback, performance assessment, progression and hiring.
Team health, dynamics and the retrospective habit that keeps them honest.
Being the team's spokesperson to the rest of engineering and to senior leadership.
Delivery
The SRE goals: what the team commits to, in what order, and why.
The support rotation and on-call model.
The platform
Remote's core infrastructure: Kubernetes, AWS, PostgreSQL, DNS and TLS, CI infrastructure.
The reliability practice: SLOs, error budgets, incident response and the observability stack.
The partnership with our Security team on threats, patching and infrastructure controls, including our audit and compliance obligations.
The vendor relationships that sit behind the platform, including renewals and commercial conversations with support from your Director.

Develop career paths and internal progression routes for technicians and site supervisors.

Ensure accurate treatment of overtime, site allowances, per diems and casual wage sheets in line with policy and the Employment Act, 2007.
Maintain the salary structure; benchmark pay and recommend annual review, increment and bonus proposals.
Manage employee benefits — medical and group life cover, WIBA and any welfare schemes.
Oversee the leave management framework and ensure leave liability is tracked and reported.
Resolve escalated payroll and benefits queries and act as the point of contact for auditors.

Act as the company's principal adviser on employee relations, ensuring fair, consistent and lawful handling of all people issues.
Chair or advise on disciplinary and grievance hearings, ensuring due process is followed.
Represent the company before the Ministry of Labour, conciliators and the Employment and Labour Relations Court.
Manage relations with any trade union, workers' representatives and joint consultative forums, including a CBA where applicable.
Coach supervisors and site managers on people management, discipline and communication.
Drive employee engagement, internal communication and welfare initiatives.
Statutory Compliance, HR Records & Risk (10%)
Ensure full compliance with the Employment Act, 2007, OSHA 2007, WIBA, the Labour Relations Act and Kenyan statutory deduction requirements.
Ensure PAYE, NSSF, SHIF/SHA, NITA levy, Housing Levy and HELB deductions and returns are filed accurately and on time.

Maintain audit-ready HR records and lead the HR component of internal, client, statutory and certification audits.
Monitor changes in labour legislation and advise management on operational and cost implications.
Ensure work permits and approvals for expatriate or specialist staff are valid and current.

Provide oversight of the administration function: front office, consumables, stationery, PPE and pantry stock.
Approve and manage service contracts with suppliers for utilities, internet, cleaning, security, courier and equipment servicing.
Oversee company vehicle management, fuel cards and driver schedules.
Ensure staff travel, accommodation and per diems for regional projects are arranged within policy and budget.
Ensure timely renewal of statutory business documents — permits, fire and OSHA certificates, insurance covers and licenses.
Ensure administrative, procurement and contract filing systems are complete and accessible.

Work with the HSE function to ensure safety standards, inductions and toolbox talks are enforced.
Ensure incidents and accidents are reported, investigated and closed out, and WIBA claims followed through.
Oversee OSHA audits, fire drills, first-aid provision and occupational health checks.
Champion employee wellness and welfare programmes across office, workshop and site teams.

Payroll reviewed, approved and released before cut-off — Target: 100% of cycles

Offer acceptance rate — Target: ≥ 85%

Performance appraisals completed within the cycle window — Target: ≥ 95% of eligible staff
HR audit findings closed within agreed timelines — Target: 100%
Personnel files complete and audit-ready — Target: ≥ 98% completeness
Disciplinary and grievance cases concluded within policy timelines — Target: ≥ 90%
Training plan delivered and NITA reimbursements claimed — Target: ≥ 90% of planned budget
Lost-time incidents on site and in the workshop — Target: Zero
HR and administration spend against approved budget — Target: Within ± 5%
Contract, license and insurance renewals actioned in advance — Target: ≥ 45 days before expiry

Higher Diploma in Human Resource Management, or CHRP (K) certification.
Full member of the Institute of Human Resource Management (IHRM) – Kenya, with a valid practising certificate.
6+ years of progressive HR experience, with at least 2 years at supervisory or managerial level.
Demonstrated working knowledge of the Employment Act 2007, Labour Relations Act, OSHA 2007, WIBA, the Data Protection Act 2019 and Kenyan statutory deduction requirements.
Proven experience running end-to-end payroll input and statutory returns for a workforce of 50+ staff.
Proficiency in MS Office (particularly Excel) and hands-on experience administering an HR/payroll system.

Master's degree in HR Management, Business Administration or Organizational Development.
Experience in construction, interiors, manufacturing, retail fit-out or a similar project-based environment.
Experience negotiating or administering a Collective Bargaining Agreement.
Experience representing an employer at the Ministry of Labour or the Employment and Labour Relations Court.
Certification or formal training in occupational safety and health.

Company Details:
Longhorn Publishers limited is a public limited liability company wholly-owned and run by Kenyans. It was incorporated in Kenya in May 1965 as Longmans of Kenya a wholly owned subsidiary of Longman Group International of the United Kingdom. At that time, it was mainly a sales promotion office handli...read moreng Longman publications published in UK. In December 1969, the company changed name to Longman Kenya Limited. During the 1970s, a limited local publishing programme was started and, around the same time, a few Kenyans were invited to join the Board of Directors.

Following the opening up of Eastern Europe after the fall of the Berlin Wall, many multinationals shifted their focus from Africa to the new markets. In addition, in the 1990’s, Kenya’s then Minister for Education banned the importation of textbooks. This forced multinationals to consider other ways of supplying the Kenyan market, including licensing, which drastically reduced their margins (as compared to supplying stock). As a result, in the 1980s Longman UK sold 40% of its shareholding to Kenyans with a further 20% being sold in 1991. Finally.in 1993, Longman UK fully divested from the company when it sold its remaining 40% shareholding to Kenyans. As a result of this divestiture, the company changed its name to Longhorn Kenya Limited.

In 2006, Longhorn undertook a rebranding exercise aimed at revitalizing the company’s image through the publishing of non-textbook reading materials. To this end, in 2007, the company launched its Sasa Sema Imprint after acquiring the intellectual property of Sasa Sema Publications Limited. Sasa Sema provides reference books, creative works, biographies and general knowledge books to cater for the unmet needs within the general readership space and thus provide a balanced diet. This initiative was in line with the company’s strategy of diversifying its product range to Include books for general readership. Longhorn is the only publisher with full approval by the Ministry of Education in 12 key subjects for secondary and primary schools.

Company Details:
We work with local communities, governments and organizations to conserve Africa’s important places.

Africa is special. Its wild lands and waters are home to incredible numbers and diversity of species living close to people. For most rural Africans, connection to place takes on unique meaning,...read moremore so than anywhere else on Earth because their daily existence depends on the productivity of their natural resources.
Challenges in Africa

Some 60 percent of Africa’s lands and waters - community property, in a sense - are managed by the people who live on them. These people are undoubtedly the most vulnerable on Earth. A continuing threat is their lack of control over the communal lands and waters they depend on for survival.

And as the people struggle, so too does the wildlife that relies on the same resources. An absence of strong institutions and governance further compounds these challenges.

Therefore, our work in Africa is focused on perfecting and exporting the best examples of community-led conservation across the continent’s vast shared lands and waters. These examples are ones that provide tangible benefits to people. Conservation has to pay to be successful.

Planning and work management
Maintain a rolling preventive maintenance programme across all trades, driven by running hours and scheduled around peak production.
Operate a single work-order system from request to close-out, so all work is recorded, prioritised, assigned and visible.
Batch work by area, trade and shutdown window so each visit and each outage delivers maximum useful work.
Reserve capacity for breakdown response while keeping the planned programme on schedule.
Asset management and lifecycle
Participate actively with ERP personnel to build and maintain a complete asset register in ERPNext, each asset uniquely identified with its cost, history and downtime recorded against it.
Weigh continued repair against replacement on cumulative cost, remaining life, downtime consequence, parts availability and residual value.
Work with Finance on depreciation, book value and disposal so the asset ledger reflects the condition of the fleet.
Identify assets nearing end of economic life in time for planned capital replacement, and prepare hire-versus-purchase analysis
Budget, cost and procurement
Own and control the maintenance budget across labour, spares, consumables, contractors and capital, and report variance with explanation.
Manage total cost of ownership, accounting for the production cost of downtime alongside direct repair cost.
Assess best-value-for-money form Original Equipment Manufacturers (OEMs) items on quality, price, lead time, warranty and support.
Set spares and critical-stock policy against lead times and criticality, and determine the balance between in-house and contracted work.
Leadership and accountability
Establish a clear departmental structure in which every member of staff reports to a named supervisor and every trade has an accountable lead.
Delegate defined authority covering work approval, release of equipment to service and expenditure within set limits.
Maintain clear communication with production and support functions, including notice of planned shutdowns, reliable recovery estimates and defined escalation thresholds.
Assign ownership of every asset, closure of every work order and conclusion of every incident investigation.
Formalise resources shared with Construction in writing, covering direction of work, funding and accountability.
Assess capability against requirement, recruit and train to close gaps, build cover across trades and conduct performance reviews.
Facilities, safety and reporting
Establish and equip trade workshops, control tools and protective equipment, and organise stores so stock is traceable and charged to the correct work order.
Own safety within maintenance operations, including permit-to-work, isolation and lock-out discipline, and verification of competence before assigning hazardous work.
Maintain statutory inspection and certification for lifting equipment, pressure systems and regulated plant, and meet Kenyan regulatory and environmental requirements.
Report monthly on availability, unplanned downtime, schedule completion, repair time, time between failures and cost, using measured data.
Represent maintenance in operations forums, advise management on emerging risk and the cost of deferral, and contribute engineering input to capital projects.

Job Title: Finance Manager - Kenya/ Somalia / Ethiopia (Kenyan Nationals only)
Job Description:
Overall Job Purpose
The Finance Manager is responsible for the effective operational financial management of the Kenya, Somalia and Ethiopia country programmes, ensuring the implementation of robust systems for accounting, compliance, budgeting and reporting, in alignment with donor and organizational requirements. The role provides financial leadership and strategic support to programme and operational teams by delivering timely financial information, strengthening financial controls and ensuring sound financial stewardship across the country programme. Reporting to and working closely with the Finance Coordinator, the Finance Manager plays a key role in ensuring sound financial stewardship and operational efficiency across the mission.
Tasks
Strategy and Vision
Actively supports the values of Johanniter and shapes programme work according to these values.
Ensures the progression and implementation of the global strategy of Johanniter International Assistance in their area of responsibility.
Contributes to the development and execution of the country strategy of Johanniter International Assistance in their area of responsibility.
Leadership
Actively lives and leads by example, upholding the Johanniter leadership principles and creating a culture where the leadership mindset can emerge and thrive, actively empowering and guiding team members to an inclusive, accountable work environment to achieve shared goals and embrace change.
This is reflected in the day-to-day activities in line with the Code of Conduct and related policies to achieve our goals.
Accounting & Financial Reporting
Manages the preparation and maintenance of financial records and reports, including general ledger, accounts payable and receivable, payroll, inventories, budgets, fixed assets and donor financial reports.
Oversees timely and accurate accounting, data entry, reconciliations and financial reporting across the country programme.
Reviews project trial balances, financial reports and account reconciliations and ensures that discrepancies are identified, investigated and resolved.
Ensures that expenses are correctly allocated to projects, cost centres, budget lines and other relevant financial dimensions in accordance with organisational and donor requirements.
Oversees review of country office and partner financial records and vouchers to ensure com-pleteness, accuracy, appropriate coding and compliance.
Oversees preparation and review of monthly, quarterly, annual and final financials and donor financial reports.
Oversees proper filing and archiving of all financial records in line with Johanniter’s financial guidelines.
Budgeting & Financial Planning
Coordinates the preparation and monitoring of country multi-annual plans and reforecasts in coordination with the management teams.
Leads the preparation, review and monitoring of project budgets in coordination with Programme and management teams.
Oversees of preparation and regular updates of donor budgets and ensures that approved budgets are correctly established, managed and updated in the SUN System.
Ensures that project staff receive accurate and timely budget variance reports and provides financial analysis and guidance to support effective decision-making.
Reviews project expenditure against approved budgets, identifies significant variances and supports reforecasts, budget revisions and fund transfers.
Prepares and reviews cash forecasts for the country programme and ensures timely availability of funds for programme and operational requirements.
Ensures that budgets and financial plans remain aligned with organisational priorities, donor requirements and available funding.
Cash & Treasury Management
Oversees cash and treasury management systems across the country programme, including cashbooks, bank accounts, advances, physical inventories and reconciliations.
Reviews cashbooks and bank records to ensure that transactions are accurately recorded, correctly coded and properly supported.
Ensures that cash counts, bank reconciliations and expenditure reconciliations are conducted regularly and that discrepancies are investigated and resolved.
Ensures timely and secure payment of salaries, per diems, advances, suppliers and statutory obligations in accordance with approved procedures.
Oversees cash forecasts and timely request of transfers from headquarters while maintaining appropriate cash balances and controls.
Identifies cash management risks and ensures that appropriate measures are implemented to safeguard financial assets and maintain continuity of operations.
Payments & Supplier Management
Oversees systems for processing supplier, staff and other authorised payments and ensures that appropriate approvals and supporting documentation are in place.
Ensures that payment processes comply with organisational procedures, donor requirements, approval thresholds and internal controls.
Reviews and authorises financial documentation within delegated authority and ensures that payments are processed accurately, transparently and on time.
Oversees payment methods including cash, cheque and bank transfers and ensures that appropriate controls are maintained.
Ensures that payment documentation is properly recorded, stamped, scanned, filed and retained in accordance with organisational requirements.
Supports the finance coordinator and management in resolving significant supplier, banking and payment-related financial issues.
Financial Compliance & Internal Controls
Ensures compliance with Johanniter financial guidelines, donor requirements, applicable nation-al regulations and internal control standards across the country programme.
Ensures that procurement, expenditure and payment processes are properly authorised, documented and compliant with organisational and donor requirements.
Oversees the implementation and effectiveness of financial controls to prevent fraud, corruption, aid diversion, financial loss and misuse of resources.
Ensures that audit, compliance and financial strengthening recommendations are implemented and monitored to completion.
Provides technical advice on financial compliance, risk management and interpretation of organisational and donor requirements.
Reports significant financial risks, irregularities, suspected fraud, corruption or control weaknesses to the Finance Coordinator and relevant management and ensures appropriate follow-up.
Partner Financial Management & Capacity Building
Oversees the review of partner financial reports, budgets, vouchers and supporting documen-tation to ensure compliance with organisational and donor requirements.
Provides financial management guidance to partners on budgeting, financial reporting, controls, procurement and donor compliance.
Monitors partner expenditure against approved budgets and identifies financial risks, variances and capacity gaps requiring management attention.
Supports partner assessments and develops or oversees financial capacity-strengthening initiatives based on identified needs.
Ensures that partner financial, HR and administrative systems and records meet applicable compliance, accountability and reporting standards.
Supports the resolution of significant partner financial issues and ensures that agreed corrective actions are followed up.
People Management
Leads, supervises and develops the finance team, ensuring clear responsibilities, effective work planning and delivery of agreed objectives.
Establishes and monitors team work plans and ensures that finance activities are appropriately prioritised and resourced.
Conducts performance management, coaching and regular feedback and ensures that staff receive appropriate support and development opportunities.
Identifies finance team capacity and skills gaps and leads appropriate training, mentoring and professional development initiatives.
Participates in recruitment, selection and onboarding of finance staff and ensures effective integration into the finance function.
Promotes an inclusive, respectful and equitable working environment, ensuring equal oppor-tunities, diversity and non-discrimination within the finance team.
Administrative Responsibilities
Oversees the maintenance of finance and related administrative filing systems and ensures that records are complete, accurate, secure and accessible to authorised personnel.
Ensures timely coordination and submission of financial and administrative documentation required by management, country office, HQ, donors and other relevant stakeholders.
Ensures that confidential financial and administrative information is appropriately protected and managed.
Coordinates with HR, administration, logistics, programme and other departments on matters with financial and administrative implications.
Ensures that statutory financial and administrative obligations are appropriately followed up and documented.
Performs other finance-related management and administrative duties within the scope of the position as assigned by the supervisor.
Professional Qualification and Experience
Essential
University Degree in Finance, Accounting or any Business-related qualification from a recognized institution.
Full professional qualification in CPA(K) or ACCA.
A member of accounting professional body with good standing.
At least six years’ experience in a similar position with progressively increasing responsibility.
Experience in financial management, budgeting, reporting and compliance within an NGO, INGO or similar organisation.
Experience supervising and developing finance staff.
Experience working with NGOs or international organizations.
Experience in partner financial management and financial capacity strengthening.
Desirable
Experience working with donor-funded projects and managing donor financial requirements.
Knowledge of national financial regulations and international accounting or auditing standards.
Experience supporting internal and external audits and financial risk management.
Experience in SUN system of accounting.
Experience managing multi-currency grants from major donors.
Experience managing multi-country operations.
Skills
Strong analytical, financial planning, problem-solving and decision-making skills.
Strong leadership and people management skills, including coaching, mentoring and perfor-mance management.
Able to organise, plan ahead and prioritise multiple tasks while meeting deadlines.
Excellent communication skills, including the ability to prepare and present financial information and draft clear financial documents.
Able to provide sound financial advice and communicate complex financial information to non-finance colleagues.
High level of integrity, discretion, accountability and professional judgement.
Flexible and able to adapt to changing operational and organisational requirements.
Commitment to diversity, inclusion, gender equality and respectful teamwork.
Able to build effective working relationships with internal and external stakeholders.
Able to travel to the responsible countries and work in challenging or basic conditions where required.
Fluent in English; knowledge of local languages will be an added advantage.

Job Title: Executive Assistant to the Executive Director
Job Description:
Job Purpose
The Executive Assistant provides high-level executive, administrative and coordination support to the Executive Director (ED) to facilitate the effective functioning of the Executive Office and implementation of organizational priorities. The position administratively reports to the Human Resources Department and functionally reports to the Executive Director. The Executive Director provides day-to-day functional direction, sets work priorities and oversees deliverables relating to the Executive Office, while Human Resources provides administrative oversight in accordance with the Hospital’s employment policies and procedures.
The role supports the Executive Director in coordinating management activities, monitoring key decisions and action points, preparing executive reports and briefing materials, facilitating communication with internal and external stakeholders, and ensuring timely follow-up on matters requiring the Executive Director’s attention.
The Executive Assistant serves as a key coordination link between the Executive Director, Management Team, Heads of Departments and external stakeholders while maintaining the highest standards of confidentiality, professionalism and discretion.
Key Responsibilities
Executive Office Coordination
Coordinate the day-to-day activities and priorities of the Executive Director’s Office.
Manage and coordinate the Executive Director’s calendar, meetings, appointments and official engagements.
Review and prioritize matters requiring the Executive Director’s attention and ensure appropriate follow-up.
Coordinate information and documentation submitted to the Executive Director by departments and other stakeholders.
Maintain an effective system for tracking correspondence, approvals, decisions and pending matters within the Executive Office.
Ensure that the Executive Director is appropriately briefed and prepared for scheduled meetings and engagements.
Management and Strategic Coordination
Support the Executive Director in coordinating activities and priorities involving members of the Management Team and Heads of Departments.
Track management decisions, commitments and action points and follow up with responsible officers on implementation within agreed timelines.
Maintain an Executive Office action tracker and provide regular updates on outstanding matters.
Coordinate submission of departmental reports, management updates and other information required by the Executive Director.
Escalate delayed or outstanding action items to the Executive Director as appropriate.
Executive Reporting and Decision Support
Prepare briefs, summaries, reports, presentations and other executive documents required by the Executive Director.
Conduct research and compile relevant information to support management discussions and decision-making.
Review documents submitted to the Executive Office for completeness and ensure relevant supporting information is available before presentation to the Executive Director.
Consolidate information and reports from various departments as directed by the Executive Director.
Support preparation of management reports and other strategic documentation.
Maintain appropriate records of key executive decisions and directives for follow-up.
Meetings and Follow-Up
Coordinate Management Team and other meetings convened by the Executive Director.
Liaise with relevant departments to prepare and circulate meeting agendas and supporting documents.
Record minutes, decisions and action points where required.
Maintain an action tracker arising from meetings and follow up with responsible officers to ensure timely implementation.
Provide the Executive Director with updates on the status of agreed actions.
Coordinate logistical requirements for meetings hosted by the Executive Director.
Stakeholder Coordination and Communication
Serve as a coordination link between the Executive Director and Management Team, Heads of Departments and other internal stakeholders.
Facilitate timely communication of the Executive Director’s instructions, decisions and priorities to relevant officers.
Liaise professionally with external stakeholders, partners, institutions, service providers and other parties engaging with the Executive Director’s Office.
Coordinate responses and follow-up on official correspondence addressed to the Executive Director.
Ensure appropriate communication protocols are maintained within the Executive Office.
Correspondence and Documentation
Draft, review and prepare official correspondence, reports, presentations, memos and other documents on behalf of the Executive Director.
Maintain organized and secure electronic and physical records for the Executive Office.
Ensure documents requiring the Executive Director’s review or approval are appropriately organized and presented.
Maintain accurate records of incoming and outgoing Executive Office correspondence.
Ensure proper filing, retrieval and archiving of Executive Office documentation.
Executive Engagements and Travel Coordination
Coordinate the Executive Director’s official travel arrangements, meetings and external engagements.
Prepare comprehensive itineraries, meeting schedules and relevant briefing materials.
Liaise with internal and external parties regarding the Executive Director’s official engagements.
Coordinate logistical arrangements for official functions, conferences and events attended or hosted by the Executive Director.
Ensure appropriate follow-up on matters arising from external engagements.
Confidentiality and Governance
Handle confidential, sensitive and privileged organizational information with a high level of discretion.
Maintain confidentiality of management discussions, employee information, business information and other sensitive matters handled through the Executive Office.
Ensure Executive Office records and documents are appropriately secured and accessed only by authorized persons.
Support adherence to hospital policies, management protocols and established governance processes.
Exercise sound judgment when handling sensitive correspondence and matters requiring escalation.
Executive Office Administration
Ensure the Executive Office operates efficiently, professionally and in an organized manner.
Coordinate visitors and official engagements involving the Executive Director.
Maintain appropriate office systems, records and administrative resources.
Perform other executive coordination duties reasonably assigned by the Executive Director in support of organizational objectives.
Role Requirements
Minimum Qualifications
Bachelor’s degree in Business Administration, Management, Human Resource Management, Public Administration, Healthcare Management or another relevant field.
Professional training in executive administration, corporate governance, project management or a related area will be an added advantage.
Experience
At least three (3) years of relevant experience in an Executive Assistant, Executive Office, management coordination or similar role.
Experience supporting senior executives or senior management in a healthcare or corporate environment will be an added advantage.

Job Description:
Purpose
The Senior Associate Engineer role performs infrastructure related activities to ensure reliable and efficient operation of the technical infrastructure. This is achieved through maintenance, testing and surveillance of all assets installed.
The Senior Associate Engineer is responsible for trouble shooting, assembly and day to day scheduling of maintenance tasks.
The role provides technical, preventative maintenance, repairs, installation and customer service support in order to adhere to agreed SLAs with our clients and to maximize client satisfaction.
Job Magnitude
Latitude-This role reports to the Area Facility Manager, working in the operations teams in collaboration with all other departments. External contacts include Clients and Suppliers.
Level of Impact- The role is critical in maintaining the reliability and efficiency of data center operations. The Senior Site Engineer role:
Ensures the stability and reliability of critical assets supporting customer equipment (availability).
Maintains operational efficiency and support agreed customer SLAs.
Coordinates maintenance tasks to mitigate unplanned maintenance and failures.
Contributes to maintaining a clean and organized data center environment.
Duties and Responsibilities
Operations and Compliance
Coordinate and execute equipment or system switching procedures as required, ensuring seamless transitions and minimal disruption to data center operations.
Contribute to the DC operating energy efficiency and implement assigned optimization measures.
Provide solutions for site management and adhere to SLAs agreed in customer contracts.
Ensure site overall appearance and cleanliness, escalating shortfalls when necessary.
Proactively indicate and report if SLAs are in danger of being breached.
Ensure all work is carried out within a 'safe system' and approved work processes, complying with best practice standards and legal requirements.
Lead and manage projects to identify root causes of facility issues, acting as an escalation point for more junior team members.
Handle technically complex and challenging situations, troubleshooting, and providing solutions for potential critical infrastructure availability.
Drive adherence to company safety policies, operational efficiency, and core values.
Ensure compliance with industry standards and legal requirements.
Perform on-call duties and manage incidents as necessary.
Document progress, issues, and results, and implement improvement measures.
Demonstrate advanced proficiency in technical skills pertinent to the role, covering troubleshooting and maintenance tasks.
Maintenance and Repair Works
Guide junior engineers in maintenance and repairs of DC equipment and building
Execute maintenance and repairs of building and equipment and document it in a timely manner.
Manage maintenance and repair operations, including coordination of contractors.
Supervise contractors and suppliers installing and maintaining critical DC equipment
Responsible for trouble shooting, assembly, and support the day-to-day scheduling of Maintenance activities.
Act as a point of escalation for technical troubleshooting of equipment during maintenance and repairs.
Make decisions with respect to maintenance and repairs tasks withing the set operations guidelines.
On-call duties and Incident Management
Day to day site monitoring and surveillance of DC building and infrastructure.
Incident management in close cooperation with the supervisor in charge.
Support and when mandated responsible for activating and executing Emergency Operating Procedures where necessary.
Acts as first line of response on alarms and handle or escalate alarms according to guidelines.
Documentation and Reporting
Document progress, issues, and results to support audits and customer inquiries.
Report and document operational standard deviations, initiating improvement measures.
Record changes to data center infrastructure per change management procedures, notifying the Facility Manager.
Document progress, issues, and results of all assigned maintenance tasks.
Execute and draft MOPs and Change Requests (CR)
Health and Safety
The Senior Associate Engineer ensures adherence to all Health and Safety Measures set out to ensure all works done at the site are safe including but not limited to:
Preparation of work permits for approval by the Facility Manager
Adhering to four eye policy in all DC Operations
Preparation of Methods Operations Procedures (MOP) for Operations activities.
Performing Risk assessment before undertaking any operations and seeking relevant approvals
Preparation of Change management forms for approval by the Facility Manager.
Adhere to overall QHSE responsibility matrix
Additional Responsibilities
Execute ad hoc projects as instructed, including but not limited to fire safety initiatives, environmental sustainability, energy efficiency optimization, security enhancement, compliance audits, and technology integration.
Be an active participant and make observations & suggestions towards the improvement of the data center effectiveness and efficiency.
Perform any other tasks assigned to them by the Facility Manager or the in-charge
Qualifications and Competencies
Hard Skills
Bachelor’s degree in Electronics and Electrical Engineering, Mechanical and Mechatronics Engineering or related Engineering field.
Minimum of 6 years of experience in operations and maintenance of Electrical and/or Mechanical systems.
Skilled in troubleshooting and maintenance of fire detection and suppression systems and HVAC systems.
Skilled in operations and maintenance of UPS, Generators, Access controls and Switch gears
Excellent problem analysis skills
Strong troubleshooting skills and RCA capability
Skilled in customer communication and handling customer requests / complaints
Skilled in service-oriented software, tasks handling and administration
Skilled in Microsoft office and Service Management applications (e.g. Excel)
Soft Skills
Proactive and customer-focused mindset, showing dedication to customer service and exceeding business goals.
Has a natural drive to work.
Attention to detail and a hands-on approach to tasks, coupled with a strong drive for continuous learning and development.
Enhanced team-oriented mentality, actively contributing to team effectiveness and demonstrating adaptability and flexibility in various situations.
Effective communication skills within the team and across different levels of the organization, while exhibiting resilience and problem-solving abilities in challenging scenarios
Demonstrate strong independence and proficiency in working under minimal supervision.

inSupply Health is seeking an experienced and dynamic Manager –Health Supply Chain Transformation to lead and support the design and implementation of innovative health supply chain interventions across our operating countries.
The Manager will work closely with Ministries of Health, government agencies, private-sector clients, NGOs, donors and other partners to identify supply chain challenges and co-design practical, sustainable solutions that improve the efficiency, effectiveness and resilience of health supply chains.
The role will provide technical and functional leadership to Analysts and Senior Analysts working across health supply chain projects, while providing coaching, mentorship and quality assurance to ensure high-quality technical delivery. The successful candidate will also contribute to business development by identifying new opportunities, developing technical approaches and supporting proposals and other business development activities.

Manage in-country project implementation, identify supply chain challenges, and co-design solutions with MOH, clients, and other stakeholders to enhance supply chain performance, ensuring appropriate use of resources to deliver quality outcomes and milestones in a timely, cost-effective, and responsive manner.
Functional Leadership, Team Development and Technical Quality Assurance:
Provide functional and technical leadership to Analysts and Senior Analysts working across projects, coordinate domain inputs, and provide coaching, mentorship and guidance to maintain high standards of technical delivery. Support staff performance, career development and capability building, and provide technical quality assurance at key project milestones to ensure that work meets inSupply Health’s standards and client expectations.
Data Utilization and Analysis:
Lead data-driven problem-solving initiatives, analyse qualitative and quantitative data, and present findings to diverse audiences to inform supply chain improvements and project decision-making. Implement IMPACT team models and frameworks in data review meetings and promote the use of evidence and insights to support adaptive management and improved supply chain performance.
Stakeholder and Client Engagement:
Build and maintain effective relationships with Ministries of Health, government institutions, NGOs, donors, clients and other partners to promote data utilisation and evidence-based decision-making. Advocate for the adoption of innovative and sustainable approaches to improve supply chain performance and efficiency, and support the Project Director/Lead and Project Manager in managing significant client issues and escalations.
Innovation and Continuous Improvement:
Foster a culture of innovation and continuous improvement, integrating human-centred design, quality improvement and other appropriate methodologies to strengthen tools, approaches and strategies.
Identify opportunities for digitalisation, including transitioning to digitised LMIS and dashboards.
Explore advanced quantification tools and health products and technologies distribution models.
Support integration with national health supply chains.
Surface potential innovations and advanced technical insights for consideration by the PMU.
Business Development and Growth:
Lead in scouting for new projects and business opportunities within the health supply chain and health systems transformation space, contributing to responses to RFPs, proposals, concept notes and other business development activities. Develop technical approaches and solutions for new opportunities, build relationships with potential clients and partners, and identify opportunities to expand existing engagements and contribute to inSupply Health’s growth and reputation.
Performance Monitoring and Adaptive Learning:
Oversee and support data collection, regular data review and analysis of project and programme monitoring indicators, facilitating adaptive learning sessions and evidence-based decision-making. When assigned as Project Manager, monitor overall project implementation progress, delivery risks, budget performance and achievement of results, ensuring timely corrective actions and escalation where required.
Knowledge Management and Technical Thought Leadership:
Capture, document and share technical insights, lessons learned, good practices and innovations across projects. Contribute to the development of technical tools, methodologies, reports, knowledge products and presentations that strengthen the Supply Chain Transformation function and inSupply Health’s technical reputation.
Project Management:
When assigned as Project Manager, the position will assume responsibility for day-to-day project delivery, coordination, performance and achievement of results. The role will also contribute to business development, stakeholder engagement, innovation and continuous improvement to strengthen the growth, impact and reputation of inSupply Health.
Qualifications:
A Bachelor’s degree in Pharmacy, Public Health, Healthcare Supply Chain or a related field. A Master’s degree in a health-related field is preferred.
At least 7 years of experience in global health or development, including at least 5 years of experience in health supply chain management.
Demonstrated experience across a range of health supply chain programmes.
Strong technical experience in areas such as:
Forecasting and supply planning
Health Supply chain assessments
Logistics Management Information Systems (LMIS)
Inventory management
Storage and distribution solutions
Health supply chain strengthening
Experience working with Ministries of Health, NGOs, donors and other development partners.
Relevant professional certification in supply chain management, project management or a related field, such as APICS CSCP or PMP, is preferred; membership in a relevant professional body is required where applicable
Experience in social marketing, healthcare social enterprise, start-up or NGO health programmes is highly desirable.
Demonstrated experience in project management, business development and/or client relationship management.
Excellent oral and written communication, influencing, networking and relationship-building skills.
What We Are Looking For
Passion for improving supply chains and health systems, with a strong understanding of market dynamics.
Self-driven, creative, and flexible, with a focus on finding innovative solutions to complex problems.
Outcome-oriented, with a proven track record in effective management and driving business development.
Ability to work collaboratively while independently managing time and results, and to provide mentorship and coaching to team members.
Experience negotiating and advocating with private- and public-sector clients for the uptake of new approaches and strategies.
Awareness of private-sector trends and the ability to leverage this knowledge to support organisational success.
Commitment to continuous learning and professional growth.
Enthusiasm for actively contributing to inSupply Health’s growth and reputation.

Job Title: Agriculture, Market Systems and Climate Finance Senior Advisor
Job Description:
Job Purpose
The Agriculture, Market Systems and Climate Finance Senior Advisor will be the technical lead and focal point internally and externally for these three important connected and strategic areas of intervention for VisionFund. This role will provide technical advice on best current practice, support the development of related products, guide strategy and organisational positioning whilst supporting Resource Development for and programme management of related Agricultural, Climate and Market systems initiatives and grants.
In particular the role will manage the CrediEnterprise (a credit product supporting Agri, Climate and Market systems interventions) pilot project in nine countries in Africa and Central America as part of the THRIVE 2030 programme and ensure it delivers on its targets, while coordinating with and reporting to World Vision partners. This includes grant reporting, project management, operational delivery, capacity building of national staff and integrating this component with other interventions within the THRIVE 2030 programme.
This role will provide technical leadership positioning VisionFund for obtaining institutional funding to support its growing Agri, Climate and Market systems interventions globally. This will involve pre-positioning with appropriate donors, grant writing and supporting the Resource Development team in VisionFund with technical content in proposal development processes.
Major Responsibilities
Technical Advisory
The role will be the technical, communications and resource mobilisation lead on Agri, market systems and climate financing and the focal point internally and externally for the VisionFund network, using their industry knowledge to advise on best practice for the VFI network.
Provide technical advice to VisionFund Operations and MicroFinance Institutions in the network on Agricultural, Market Systems and Climate industry best practices
Take a leading role in VisionFund’s Internal Climate Financing working group, using their knowledge and experience to shape VisionFund strategy, products and positioning in the market.
Represent VisionFund in technical working groups such as Environmental and Climate Action forums to communicate VisionFund strategy and brand visibility within the World Vision partnership.
Resource Development
Support resource development activities for Agricultural, Climate and Market systems, supporting on grant writing, review and donor positioning
Provide technical advice and content in support of the design and writing of new and existing agricultural, market systems and climate finance grant applications
Lead VisionFund efforts on positioning our work with agricultural, climate and market systems focussed donors and opportunities
Lead efforts to leverage learnings on the implementation of CrediEnterprise in the THRIVE 2030 programme to obtain additional institutional funding
Represent the Organization in technical grant calls and donor visits as needed.
Establish a mechanism for tracking ESCA climate-finance engagements and opportunities.
Provide technical advisory on the implementation of new and ongoing institutional funding on agri/climate or green/market systems in partnership with the RDM and Operations teams.
Lead sector learning, evidence documentation and dissemination for VisionFund to support positioning and acquisition activities
Operational Delivery
Oversee implementation of CrediEnterprise as part of the THRIVE 2030 programme and other relevant agri, climate and market systems projects.
Project manage implementation of CrediEnteprise- reaching THRIVE 2030 targets, working closely with MFI Country managers and World Vision field offices.
Supervise rollout of the CrediEnterprise product training providing ongoing coaching and mentoring to MFI staff
Support the gathering of commodity profiles for the agrocalculator.
Lead the replication of standard tools and processes developed by Operations, into CE projects.

Job Description:
What you will do:
We are seeking an experienced Contact Center Solutions Specialist to implement, maintain and improve the configuration layer of our contact-center platform (Webitel) across multiple African markets: call flows, forms, queues, agents, dialers, IVRs, API integrations, automation of repetitive configuration work, and the operational dashboards and documentation that keep it all visible. The role works under the technical direction of the Regional Customer Operations Manager, alongside an infrastructure team that owns servers and platform internals and paid vendor support.
Prior Webitel experience is not required and is treated as a plus. The realistic candidate comes from an adjacent contact-center or VoIP platform (Genesys, Avaya, Asterisk, FreeSWITCH, 3CX, Twilio, VICIdial, Five9, Cisco or similar) and is trained on Webitel internally.
Key Responsibilities:
Platform configuration and implementation (core of the role):
Build, modify, test, version and document call Flow Schemas; work confidently in both the visual flow editor and the underlying JSON.
Transfer schemas and configuration between environments and country instances, using the platform REST API where it is faster and safer than manual work.
Create forms; configure queues, agents, teams, skills, buckets, calendars and outbound resources.
Configure and tune preview, progressive, predictive and outbound-IVR dialers: campaigns, retry logic, attempt limits, calendars and call outcomes.
Turn business requests into working flows. Example: a new collections campaign where customers in different DPD buckets hear different messages, route to different teams, and self-service payment is offered via an API call with an agent fallback.
Telephony (diagnosis and escalation, not configuration):
Perform first-line diagnosis of failed calls, misrouting, one-way audio and no audio: localise the fault to a flow, a platform configuration, a trunk or beyond.
Understand SIP well enough to say, for example: “This is not a schema issue. The INVITE reaches the trunk and we get a 503 back,” and route the problem to the carrier, the infrastructure team or vendor support with logs, Call-IDs, timestamps and call examples attached.
Support testing and verification when new numbers, trunks or markets are brought live.
APIs, integrations and automation:
Build and maintain webhook and REST integrations between the platform and the ERP, AI voice vendors and messaging providers; test endpoints and localise integration failures.
Automate repetitive configuration, testing and reporting tasks with scripts against the platform API and SQL.
Monitoring and reporting:
Use, maintain and extend operational Grafana dashboards for queues, dialers, trunks and campaigns; verify questioned figures against call data with SQL.
Watch dialer and queue behaviour daily; flag anomalies before the business reports them.
Documentation and escalation:
Keep the schema library and change log current; document every production change.
Escalate correctly through the appropriate channel (vendor ticket, carrier contact, chat or email): platform faults to vendor support, trunk and number faults to carriers, server and network faults to the infrastructure team, always with structured evidence and what has already been ruled out.
Out of scope:
For clarity, this role does not include: server, OS and database administration; backups, patching and infrastructure monitoring; platform internals administration (FreeSWITCH, OpenSIPS, RTPengine); SIP trunk and gateway configuration; general IT support; or platform architecture decisions. These are owned by the infrastructure team, paid vendor support and the Regional Customer Operations Manager.
Requirements
1.5 to 2+ years hands-on with any production contact-center or VoIP platform (Genesys, Avaya, Asterisk, FreeSWITCH, 3CX, Twilio, VICIdial, Five9, Cisco, Webitel or similar).
Has built or modified IVR/call-routing logic with variables and conditions; comfortable reading JSON.
Has configured queues, agents/skills and at least one dialing mode in production, and can explain retry logic and core campaign metrics (answer rate, abandonment, contact rate).
Working SIP basics for diagnosis: can describe a call setup and interpret common 4xx/5xx responses in a trunk context.
REST API basics: can build and test a request, read the response, and follow a failing integration across systems.
Careful change discipline: tests first, documents changes, no undocumented edits in production.
Clear written English for documentation and evidence-based escalations.
Willingness to be trained on Webitel and to work within a defined scope under the hiring manager’s technical direction.
A plus:
Webitel experience (administration, Flow Schemas, dialers or API).
Experience running high-volume outbound campaigns (collections, telesales, notifications) and tuning dialer parameters.
Using a platform API for configuration at scale (bulk creation, environment-to-environment transfer, scripted changes).
Basic Grafana or any SQL-backed dashboarding (Kibana, Metabase, Redash, Superset).
Python or Bash scripting against APIs.
Exposure to African carriers and their CLI/DID practices.
First-line experience diagnosing one-way audio or trunk failures, even if resolution was escalated.
Nice to have:
Wireshark/tcpdump exposure at a reading level.
Git for versioning schemas and scripts.
Exposure to AI voice bots, TTS/STT or conversational IVR.
Additional regional languages relevant to our markets.
Behavioral competencies:
Precision:
A wrong calendar or retry value silently damages a live campaign; this person checks twice and tests on a test schema first.
Evidence over opinion:
Reports “trunk X returned 503 on 41 of 60 attempts between 09:10 and 09:25, Call-IDs attached” rather than “calls are failing”.
Scope awareness:
Knows when a problem has left their layer and hands it over cleanly.
Learning appetite:
The role is a deliberate investment in someone who wants to master a specialized platform.

About the Role
We are looking for an SD-WAN NOC Engineer to monitor and support multivendor SD-WAN environments, perform first-level troubleshooting, and coordinate incident resolution while maintaining network availability and customer SLAs.
Key Responsibilities
• Monitor SD-WAN devices, WAN links, tunnels, alarms and network performance.
• Troubleshoot connectivity, packet loss, latency, routing and device issues.
• Log, prioritize and track incidents within agreed SLAs.
• Collect diagnostic information and escalate issues to L2 teams.
• Coordinate with ISPs, field engineers and customer teams for service restoration.
• Support device onboarding, replacements, post-change validation and shift handovers.
• Maintain incident updates, reports and troubleshooting documentation.
Required Skills

Job Title: Consultant, Field Enumerator, LOSHAK, Population Health
Job Description:
Job Summary.
The purpose of this role is to support data collection, i.e. conducting household interviews and deploying actigraphy for the LOSHAK study in the following counties Kakamega, Kirinyaga, Kisumu, Kitui, Mombasa, Nairobi, Nakuru & Wajir..
Terms of Reference
Specific Tasks
Participate fully in enumerator training, household mapping and listing, pilot testing, and all preparatory activities, and successfully complete the certification process.
Identify, locate, and visit assigned households and respondents according to the approved sampling procedures.
Build rapport with sampled households and participants.
Introduce the study, explain its objectives, and obtain informed consent from respondents before commencing interviews.
Administer study questionnaires and other approved data collection tools using the designated Computer-Assisted Personal Interviewing (CAPI) application.
Conduct interviews in a professional, respectful, and culturally appropriate manner while maintaining confidentiality.
Collect complete, accurate, and timely data in accordance with the study protocol and field procedures while ensuring data integrity is maintained.
Prepare and submit daily field progress reports and other required documentation.
Attend daily briefing and debriefing meetings and implement corrective actions as advised.
Report any operational, technical, ethical, security, or data quality issues encountered during fieldwork and ensure documentation.
Maintain a log and safeguard all project equipment, materials, and documents issued for fieldwork and frequently updating the Field Supervisor of their status.
Comply with all study protocols, organizational policies, and fieldwork procedures.
Perform any other field-related duties assigned by the field supervisor that are relevant to the successful implementation of the study.
Administer the multi-module LOSHAK Core and HCAP Surveys (covering demographics, healthcare utilization, household economics, and family caregiving dynamics).
Conduct complex cognitive and neuropsychological assessment batteries (e.g., the 21-item Swahili Mental State Examination, 10-word recall, and animal naming modules) with all participants, maintaining high patience and testing fidelity.
Identify instances requiring proxy informants when selected respondents experience significant cognitive or physical impairments, following standardized study rules.
Perform precise clinical, physical, and anthropometric measurements including blood pressure readings, hand-grip strength tests (using dynamometers), height, weight, waist, and hip circumferences.
Coordinate the deployment and retrieval of wearable physical activity trackers given to select participants as well as reporting any malfunctioning of devices for timely resolution
Verify that all CAPI data entries are accurate, comprehensive, logical, and structurally consistent before field submission.
Synchronize data daily with the central institutional secure server to allow real-time data monitoring and quality sweeps by the data management team.
Maintain accurate tracking logs of all field visits, callbacks (in cases where participants were absent), and refusals and communicate this to supervisors.
Resolve and/or provide clarity on all data quality issues that have been flagged for review by the DQA teams.
Requirements
Possess at least a Diploma in Statistics, Public Health, Community Health, Social Sciences, Demography, Epidemiology, Computer Science or a related field.

Company Details: Ol Pejeta is the largest black rhino sanctuary in east Africa, and home to three of the world’s last remaining northern white rhino. It is the only place in Kenya to see chimpanzees, in a Sanctuary established to rehabilitate animals rescued from the black market. It has some of the highest...read morepredator densities in Kenya, and still manages a very successful livestock programme. Ol Pejeta also seeks to support the people living around its borders, to ensure wildlife conservation translates to better education, healthcare and infrastructure for the next generation of wildlife guardians. In 2004, the ranch was purchased by the U.K.-based conservation organisation, Fauna &Flora International (FFI), with the financial backing of the Arcus Foundation, a private international philanthropic organisation founded by Jon Stryker. The land purchase was wholly funded by a $15 million donation from the Arcus Foundation, which worked in tandem with FFI and the Lewa Wildlife Conservancy to secure the 90,000 acres of open Savannah grassland and convert it to a national land trust. The conservation of the natural habitat, located in Kenya’s Laikipia Plateau, ensured the protection of existing rhino, elephant, and other wildlife populations in addition to captive chimpanzees living in a 300-acre sanctuary. The Arcus Foundation also gave $12 million to fund capital and institutional development costs at the conservancy. That initial injection of funding allowed Ol Pejeta Conservancy to fulfill its business model as a Kenyan-owned operation benefiting local community development and economic growth in addition to its impact on conservation. Today, the Arcus Foundation continues to support the conservancy through its membership on the Board of Trustees and the funding of various initiatives. In 2014, Ol Pejeta achieved IUCN Green List status, one of only two conservancies in Africa to be awarded this. IUCN Green Listing aims to define excellence in managing valuable natural areas. We have also been awarded the TripAdvisor Certificate of Excellence three years running - a testament to the incredible experiences treasured by all who visit Ol Pejeta. In 2015, we published our 2020 Management Plan - which was developed by our staff in consultation with a range of stakeholders, and sets out our vision for the years leading up to 2020, outlining the major projects that will help us to deliver our vision. We want to become an innovative and sustainable model that conserves biodiversity (particularly endangered species) and contributes to economic growth and the improvement of the livelihoods of rural communities.

Job Title: Aftersales Central Planning & Business Performance Analyst
Job Description:
Role Purpose
The Aftersales Central Planning & Business Performance Analyst is responsible for centralized planning, spare parts demand management, order consolidation, supply-pipeline visibility, spare parts costing analysis and business performance analytics across Spiro Aftersales operations in Africa.
The role acts as the central analytical and planning link between Aftersales Country Leadership Teams, Procurement, Supply Chain, Finance, Warehousing, Quality, Service Operations and the Head of Aftersales – Africa. It establishes one source of truth for demand, inventory, open orders, supply pipeline, landed cost, revenue and key operational performance metrics.
The position is expected to move Aftersales from reactive ordering and historical reporting toward forecast-driven replenishment, proactive risk management and data-led business performance management that improves parts availability, fleet uptime, working-capital efficiency and profitability.
Key Responsibilities
Central Aftersales Planning
Coordinate the consolidated Aftersales planning cycle across all operating countries.
Work closely with Aftersales Country Leadership Teams to translate fleet growth, bike deployment, service demand and network expansion into executable Aftersales plans.
Consolidate country requirements into a Pan-African planning view and maintain monthly, quarterly and annual rolling forecasts.
Standardize planning templates, assumptions, calendars and reporting methodologies across countries.
Identify future capacity, inventory and supply risks before they impact operations.
Spare Parts Forecasting & Demand Planning
Own central spare parts forecasting using Units in Operation (UIO), historical consumption, deployment forecasts, service intervals, failure rates, warranty trends, replacement ratios, bike model mix and network growth.
Develop forecasts at country, bike model and SKU/part-number level.
Review forecast versus actual consumption and drive continuous improvement in forecast accuracy.
Define and monitor safety stock, reorder parameters and critical-parts requirements.
Segment inventory into fast-, medium-, slow- and non-moving categories and highlight abnormal consumption or stock-out risks.
Country Order Consolidation
Receive, challenge and validate country spare parts requirements before consolidation.
Validate requirements against available stock, open POs, goods in transit, historical consumption, forecast demand, safety stock and existing pipeline.
Consolidate country requirements to optimize MOQ utilization without creating unnecessary overstock.
Maintain the master consolidated order tracker and ensure approved requirements are submitted within the agreed planning calendar.
Procurement & Supply Pipeline Tracking
Work closely with Procurement and Supply Chain to track orders end-to-end: Requirement → Consolidation → Approval → PR → PO → Supplier Confirmation → Payment → Production → Balance Payment → Shipment → Clearance → Transport → Receipt → Verification → Binning → Availability.
Maintain a centralized Pan-African procurement and supply-pipeline tracker.
Track supplier commitments, production status, shipment ETAs and lead-time performance.
Coordinate visibility of payment dependencies with Finance and Procurement and escalate delays that threaten service operations or fleet uptime.
Analyse actual order-to-availability lead time versus target and identify bottlenecks.
Spare Parts Costing & Commercial Analysis
Conduct spare parts costing analysis covering supplier purchase price, freight, duties and taxes, clearance, inland logistics and total landed cost.
Analyse cost variances against budget, standard cost and prior purchases.
Track selling price, gross margin and margin movement by part, category, model and country.
Identify parts with inadequate or negative margins and provide data-backed recommendations.
Support pricing reviews, localization, alternative sourcing and make/buy decisions with Finance, Procurement and Aftersales Leadership.
Inventory Performance & Working Capital
Monitor inventory value, accuracy, parts availability, fill rate, stock turns, days of inventory, ageing, excess stock, obsolete stock and stock-outs.
Develop country inventory-health dashboards and identify opportunities for inter-country stock redistribution.
Recommend actions to reduce excess and obsolete inventory while protecting service levels.
Balance parts availability against working-capital efficiency and track inventory investment against budget.
Aftersales Business Performance Analytics
Develop consolidated analytics for bike inflow, job cards, TAT, MTTR, fleet uptime, grounded bikes, First Time Fix, repeat repairs, technician productivity, workshop productivity, Service App utilization, parts consumption and warranty performance.
Analyse country performance against targets and benchmarks, identifying gaps, trends, root causes, risks and improvement opportunities.
Translate operational data into clear management actions rather than reporting numbers only.
Revenue & Financial Performance Analytics
Consolidate spare parts revenue, labour revenue, total Aftersales revenue, gross margin, cost per repair, revenue per job card and revenue per service location.
Analyse budget versus actual performance and identify revenue leakage and commercial growth opportunities.
Support annual budgets, rolling forecasts and profitability analysis.
Country Performance Partnership
Act as a central planning and performance business partner to Aftersales Country Leadership Teams.
Conduct structured country performance reviews, challenge forecast assumptions and validate requirements.
Support country corrective action plans and track agreed actions, owners and timelines to closure.
Identify best practices for cross-country replication and escalate material risks to the Head of Aftersales – Africa.
Management Reporting & Executive Dashboards
Develop standardized Pan-African Aftersales dashboards and weekly, monthly and quarterly management reports.
Support Monthly Business Reviews (MBRs), Quarterly Business Reviews and executive presentations.
Provide country-versus-country comparisons, actual versus target/budget views, key risks, root causes and corrective actions.
Automate recurring reports wherever practical.
Data Governance & Digital Systems
Support effective utilization of SAP/ERP, Service App, inventory systems, CRM, Power BI, Excel/Power Query and other Aftersales platforms.
Maintain standardized KPI definitions and conduct data-quality and reconciliation checks.
Drive improved reporting discipline, traceability and automation across countries.
Continuous Improvement
Analyse the end-to-end Aftersales planning and order-to-availability process to identify bottlenecks and non-value-adding activities.
Support transition from reactive ordering to forecast-driven replenishment.
Develop analytical business cases for process improvements and track realized benefits.
Promote fact-based and data-driven decision-making across Aftersales.
.Qualifications
Bachelor’s degree in Supply Chain Management, Business Analytics, Engineering, Statistics, Economics, Finance, Business Administration, Operations Management or a related discipline.
Professional certification in Supply Chain, Demand Planning, Business Analytics, Power BI or Inventory Management is an added advantage.
Experience
Minimum 10 years’ relevant professional experience.
Strong preference for experience in automotive, two-wheeler, electric mobility, automotive spare parts, automotive distribution or manufacturing/service operations.
Demonstrable experience in spare parts forecasting, demand planning, inventory analysis, procurement coordination and/or business performance analytics.
Strong understanding of the relationship between fleet population, service demand, spare parts consumption, inventory investment, vehicle uptime and Aftersales revenue.
Experience supporting multiple countries, branches, dealerships or service locations is highly desirable.
Exposure to SAP/ERP environments is strongly preferred.
Technical Competencies
Advanced Microsoft Excel
Power BI and Power Query
Demand forecasting and inventory modelling
Spare parts planning
Costing and landed-cost analysis
Financial and margin analysis
Procurement pipeline management
Data visualization and executive dashboards
ERP/SAP
Strong PowerPoint capability
SQL knowledge is an advantage

Marketing & Brand Management

Build the Sidian Bank Brand to ensure that the bank is top of mind as an enterprise bank.

Minimize customer attrition by offering the required solutions to the customer and proactively responding to queries and complaints.

Identify financial and non-financial requirements of HNW clients by conducting financial needs analysis

Set performance objectives and measures of success for in liaison with the Branch Manager and providing regular feedback from staff appraisal processes.
Responsible for identifying personal career path in the bank.
Keeping abreast with staff communications, attending staff meetings – morning huddles and weekly progress meetings.
Preparing an annual Personal Development Plan (PDP) and ensuring its actualization.
Adherence to the banks policies and procedures, dress code, code of conduct, HR policies and procedures and follows laid down grievance and disciplinary procedure to ensure a conducive work environment.
Closure of identified deficiencies from concluded audits, correction within stipulated timelines, and ensure no repeat findings.
Adhere to the set number of learning/training hours are achieved for self and direct reports, through E-learning and Internal training activities.

Customer onboarding as per policy.
Portfolio management as per policy.
Credit appraisal and debt monitoring for accounts in PAR or NPL as per policy.
KYC compliance as per policy.

University degree or above in a relevant business discipline e.g. business administration or finance.
WORK EXPERIENCE
At least 7 years’ experience in retail banking and/or commercial banking including a minimum of 4 years sales experience.
SKILLS & COMPETENCIES
Sound knowledge of Retail Banking/SME products, services and processes together with exposure in retail banking branch operations or customer service delivery.
Profound understanding of retail market, key competitors and offerings as well as our competitive edges to win quality customers.
Thorough understanding of CBK regulatory framework and pertinent regulations impacting corporate customers.
Strong leadership, marketing, sales and management skills.
Highly effective communicator with excellent interpersonal and motivational skills.

Excellent relationship building and stakeholder management skills.

Diploma in Banking – AKIB (added advantage)

Ensure physical and digital learning resources such as workbooks, slides, handouts, reports (training and evaluation), learning aids are filed and easily accessible.
Support the development and maintenance of vibrant learning resources repositories to serve AWARD training courses
Assist in collecting, organizing, and categorizing training materials and reports.
Ensure consistency, quality, and accuracy of information stored in knowledge systems.
Gather reports, analyze participants’ and facilitators’ feedback, and share with relevant units
Ensure current virtual learning platforms and digital collaboration tools are updated, available, and accessible when required
Assist with analyzing learning portal usage and identifying gaps or improvement areas.
Provide support to staff in accessing or retrieving training-related materials.

Customize existing pre-course activities
Communicate pre-course activities and requirements to participants
Administer assessments test surveys
Generate reports
Disseminate the reports/feedback
Follow up on participants’ post-training requirements/expected outputs.
Undertake continuous improvement and innovation by conducting periodic curriculum reviews based on participant feedback, learning analytics, and organizational priorities.
Review training materials to ensure consistency, instructional quality, branding, and accessibility.

Assist in facilitating communication between training partners, participants, and AWARD.
Schedule and document meetings with stakeholders.
Follow up on action items, requests from participants, trainers and related stakeholders.
Maintain a contact database of key stakeholders and partners.
Prepare formal congratulatory messages to AWARD training alumni and stakeholders for key milestones as and when necessary.
Follow up on disputes or complaints from participants and trainers and have them addressed by the relevant units/office

Master’s degree in education, or training and development, and/or related fields
At least 5 years of progressive experience in capacity development, managing training programs, preferably in an international or regional organization.
Professional certification in virtual facilitation and learning technologies, e-learning instructional design
Demonstrated experience providing technical support in virtual and blended learning using digital learning technologies and learner engagement techniques.
Experience administering a Learning Management System (LMS).
Experience providing technical support during live online events

Ability to manage and lead hybrid teams.
Expertise and experience in delivering training or capacity development intervention on gender-responsive approaches in agrifood systems, would be an added advantage.

forward-thinking Actuarial Manager

Job Description:

Lead IFRS 17 Systemization and Reporting
Champion automation and systemization of IFRS 17 actuarial reporting processes for Life and General Insurance entities.
Collaborate with Finance and IT to streamline data integration between actuarial and accounting systems.

Drive continuous system improvement and oversee upgrades and enhancements.

Lead automation initiatives to improve actuarial data management and reporting efficiency.

Work closely with Group Finance, Risk, and IT to embed actuarial systems into wider Group processes.
Provide mentorship, training, and technical guidance on model governance and system best practices.
Actively contribute to Group Actuarial governance and continuous improvement forums.
Governance, Risk, and Compliance
Ensure actuarial models and reports comply with Group policies, professional standards, and regulatory requirements.
Maintain comprehensive documentation of actuarial methodologies and assumptions.
Support internal and external model validation and implement improvement recommendations.

Qualifications

Technical Excellence:
Advanced analytical, modelling, and problem-solving skills with a strong systems orientation.

Passion for automation, digital transformation, and continuous improvement.
