Ability to collaborate effectively with Finance, Risk, and IT teams across multiple jurisdictions.
Strategic Thinking:
Capacity to link actuarial insights to business outcomes and decision-making.
Integrity & Accuracy:
Commitment to precision, auditability, and governance standards.
Leadership & Mentorship:
Willingness to guide and upskill teams in actuarial systems and processes.
Resilience & Agility:
Comfortable working in a dynamic environment with evolving regulatory and business needs.

Job Description:
Overall Purpose
The Systems Auditor provides independent assurance and advisory on the adequacy, effectiveness, and security of information systems, IT governance, and technology controls across the Kenya Red Cross Society (KRCS) commercial entities, including Boma Hotels, Eplus, Switch TV, and Boma International Hospitality College (BIHC). The role supports business continuity and operational efficiency by evaluating IT risks, cybersecurity, ERP controls and compliance with information systems policies and standards.
Key Responsibilities
Audit Planning & Execution
Conduct financial, operational, compliance, investigative, IT, and systems audits in line with approved audit plans and professional standards.
Identify operational inefficiencies, control gaps, process improvement opportunities and recommend corrective actions.
Governance, Risk & Internal Controls
Evaluate governance, risk management, internal controls and IT controls to identify weaknesses and improvement opportunities.
Review controls to ensure the accuracy, integrity, security and availability of organizational information.
IT & Systems Audit
Review IT governance, cybersecurity, information security, business continuity, disaster recovery and change management controls.
Review ERP systems, application controls, user access, system configurations and automated controls.
Review IT projects, system implementations, upgrades, and integrations to ensure adequate controls are in place.
Use data analytics and CAATs to identify anomalies, control weaknesses, fraud risks, and unusual transactions.
Compliance & Investigations
Assess compliance with policies, laws, regulations, contractual obligations, ICT requirements, software licensing, and data protection standards.
Conduct fraud and investigative audits and report suspected irregularities or policy violations.
Reporting, Follow-Up & Advisory
Prepare audit reports, communicate findings and follow up on implementation of agreed recommendations.
Advise management on internal controls, risk management, cybersecurity, IT governance and emerging technology risks.
Person Specifications
Academic Qualifications
Bachelor's Degree in Information Technology, Computer Science, Information Systems, Computer Engineering or a related field.
Professional Qualifications
CISA (Certified Information Systems Auditor) is required.
Relevant certifications such as CISSP, CISM, CRISC, ISO 27001 Lead Auditor/Implementer, or CPA(K) will be an added advantage.
Membership in ISACA or another relevant professional body.
Experience
Minimum of four (4) years' experience in IT audit
Experience auditing ERP systems and business applications such as Sun Systems, Navision, Opera, Microsoft Dynamics or similar platforms.
Experience with data analytics, IT general controls (ITGCs), application controls and systems implementation reviews.
Competencies, Skills and Knowledge
Strong knowledge of IT auditing standards, COBIT, ISO 27001, IT General Controls (ITGCs), cybersecurity and risk management.
Proficiency in audit data analytics and CAATs (e.g., ACL, IDEA, Power BI, SQL, Excel).
Knowledge of cloud computing, network security, databases, ERP systems and data privacy regulations.
Strong analytical, report writing, and problem-solving skills.
Excellent communication and stakeholder management skills.
High integrity, professionalism, and ability to maintain confidentiality.
Ability to manage multiple assignments and work collaboratively across diverse business units.
Compliance and Risk Management
Ensure adherence to financial policies, procedures and internal controls.
Support implementation of audit recommendations.
Monitor compliance with donor and statutory requirements.
Support periodic asset verification exercises.
Identify and report financial and operational risks.

Company Details: Established in 1952, the Aga Khan Hospital in Kisumu is part of the Aga Khan Health Services (AKHS). It is a 61-bed acute care facility managed by qualified professionals who include experienced, full-time resident doctors and consultants. The hospital's objectives are to provide high quality...read more, cost-effective health care to the population of Western Kenya and neighbouring countries. The Hospital provides general medicine services, specialist clinics and high-tech diagnostic services and has a well-equipped 24-hour emergency Casualty Department. It is also part of the AKHS international referral system, with links to the Aga Khan University Hospital in Nairobi and Karachi respectively. History On 26 February 1951, Prince Aly Khan laid the foundation for the Aga Khan Dispensary and Maternity Home. The home had an 8-bed general ward. In 1960, the dispensary was extended to incorporate two general wards with a total of 17 beds and an outpatient department. A small laboratory was established in 1975 and a portable X-ray machine purchased. Patient activity levels continued to increase. By 1979, the average bed occupancy was over 100 percent, which indicated a need for expansion. In 1991, the hospital had 55 beds, piped oxygen gas was available, an administration block was completed and physiotherapy services were introduced. By 1992, the bed capacity was increased to 76 with a paediatric ward, a VIP wing and an acute care unit. Presently the hospital offers services in the areas of Medicine, Surgery, Paediatrics, Obstetrics & Gynaecology and Acute Care. It also provides 24-hour emergency / ambulatory services. This is further supported by basic to intermediate specialised investigations both in laboratory and radiology and a well-stocked pharmacy, all on a 24-hour basis. The Hospital has introduced haemodialysis, dental, ophthalmology, endoscopy, histopathology and imaging services, including image-guided non-vascular intervention, CT scans and Doppler ultrasounds. The significant strengthening of the diagnostic departments has been through the recruitment of expatriate consultants from India a radiologist and a pathologist. Aga Khan Health Services AKHS has facilities in Kenya and Tanzania that provide care to over 600,000 patients annually in both rural and urban, and preventive and curative contexts. Its hospitals provide an increasingly comprehensive range of high-quality clinical services. Healthcare Activities of the Aga Khan Development Network AKHS activities are conducted in concert with other health-related activities of the Aga Khan Development Network (AKDN). The overall aim is to raise the health status of people in East Africa and elsewhere in the developing world. In current projects, emphasis is on strengthening health systems development. The Aga Khan Foundation (AKF), with branches in Kenya, Tanzania, and Uganda, works with a variety of grantees, including AKHS, to improve the health of vulnerable population groups, especially mothers and children, and promote health services development on the national and regional levels. AKF and AKHS have been joined in their work in health care in East Africa by the Aga Khan University's Faculty of Health Sciences, which offers accredited professional training, especially for nurses and doctors, and conducts a variety of research programmes focused on the health problems of developing nations. The AKDN aims to assist countries in the building of effective, sustainable health systems linking different kinds of services and levels of care. For more information, please visit the AKDN website.

Job Description:
ABOUT THE OPPORTUNITY & RESPONSIBILITIES
Inkomoko is strengthening its approach to climate resilience, circular economy, and sustainable enterprise development. We are seeking a senior consultant to lead an initial Circular Economy Pilot with local social sector organizations while helping build the institutional foundations for Inkomoko’s longer-term climate and Environmental, Social and Governance (ESG) capability.
The immediate focus will be on 15 high-potential refugee-led organizations (RLOs) in Kenya and Ethiopia, supporting them to identify, design, finance, and implement income-generating, climate-smart circular economy interventions focused on food security, renewable energy, and waste management.
However, the mandate extends beyond successful delivery of the pilot. The consultant will develop the content, tools, processes, workflows, partnerships, and learning required to enable Inkomoko to integrate climate and environmental considerations more systematically into its enterprise-development model and evolving impact architecture.
This is therefore a strategic, hands-on institution-building assignment. The successful candidate will need to move between strategy and execution: working directly with RLOs, building the capability of Inkomoko teams, developing practical tools and systems, engaging technical and financing partners, and translating learning from the pilot into institutional capabilities that can be applied beyond the initial project. This will be a 12 month Consultancy.
Key Responsibilities
Lead the Circular Economy Pilot
Own the end-to-end delivery of the Circular Economy Pilot with 15 selected RLOs.
Design and facilitate an intervention-development process that enables RLOs to identify viable, climate-smart and income-generating opportunities.
Support RLOs to develop high-quality intervention proposals, including business models, implementation plans, financing requirements, risks, timelines, and expected outcomes.
Work closely with Investment and relevant Inkomoko teams to assess interventions and facilitate appropriate financing.
Provide technical oversight and coaching during implementation.
Ensure the 15 RLOs implement viable interventions and generate measurable economic, employment, environmental, and resilience outcomes.
Build Climate & Circular Economy Capability within Inkomoko
Develop practical climate and circular economy content, tools, workflows, and guidance that can be embedded into Inkomoko’s existing RLO and enterprise-development programming.
Develop and deliver a climate resilience module and train Inkomoko staff to deliver it effectively.
Build staff capability through training-of-trainers, field observation, coaching, and quality assurance.
Develop practical approaches for identifying climate-related opportunities and risks within enterprise and social-sector programming.
Create reusable tools and processes that enable country teams to integrate climate considerations without requiring specialist support for every intervention.
Lay the Foundations for Inkomoko’s Climate & ESG Capability
Work with BGS, MERL, Program Design & Innovation, Investment, and relevant leadership to identify how climate, environmental sustainability, and ESG considerations should progressively be integrated into Inkomoko’s impact model.
Develop an initial institutional roadmap for climate and ESG integration, identifying priority capabilities, systems, standards, data requirements, partnerships, and ownership.
Identify opportunities to integrate climate resilience, resource efficiency, circular business models, and environmental considerations into enterprise development.
Develop recommendations for how climate and ESG considerations can inform programme design, enterprise support, investment, measurement, and organizational decision-making.
Distil learning from the pilot into an enterprise-level Climate/ESG playbook or foundational framework that Inkomoko can further develop after the consultancy.
Build Partnerships and Technical Ecosystems
Identify and develop relationships with technical experts, private-sector actors, financial institutions, governments, funders, research institutions, and other ecosystem partners relevant to climate and circular economy.
Identify opportunities for technical assistance, financing, market linkages, innovation, and co-investment.
Build partnerships that can help RLOs and entrepreneurs move from pilot interventions to commercially viable and scalable models.
Bring external knowledge, market intelligence, and emerging climate practices into Inkomoko.
Evidence, Learning & Scale
Work with MERL to develop appropriate baseline, monitoring, outcome, and learning approaches for the pilot.
Track implementation, income generation, employment, resilience, and relevant environmental outcomes.
Generate practical evidence on which circular economy interventions are viable, for whom, under what conditions, and with what level of support.
Document lessons, case studies, tools, and recommendations to inform future programming and investment.
Develop a clear scale recommendation for Inkomoko based on evidence from the pilot.
Cross-functional Leadership
Build coalitions across BGS, Investment, MERL, Program Design & Innovation, Country Leadership, and other relevant teams to embed climate thinking into existing systems rather than create a standalone project.
Provide regular strategic updates to Inkomoko leadership, highlighting progress, risks, decisions required, and opportunities.
Influence across functions without relying on formal authority and build internal ownership of the emerging climate agenda.
EXPECTED RESULTS;
The consultant will be accountable for delivering the following immediate results:
Circular Economy Pilot
15 RLOs complete a structured circular intervention-design process.
15 RLOs receive appropriate financing and implement climate-smart circular interventions.
Interventions generate measurable income and employment opportunities, with an ambition of 3,000 jobs created.
Participating RLOs demonstrate improved climate resilience and organizational capability.
Institutional Capability
In addition to the pilot results, the consultant will leave Inkomoko with:
A practical climate resilience and circular economy curriculum and delivery package.
Standardized intervention-design tools, processes, and workflows.
A Climate & ESG integration roadmap for Inkomoko.
Foundational guidance for integrating climate and environmental considerations into enterprise development and the evolving impact model.
A network of strategic technical and ecosystem partners.
Evidence and recommendations to inform future scale, investment, and institutionalization.
Internal staff capability sufficient to continue and expand the work beyond the consultancy.
Requirements
WHO WE ARE LOOKING FOR
We are looking for a climate and sustainability leader who can both build and do. This person should be comfortable designing strategy and systems at an institutional level while working directly with organizations and teams to turn ideas into viable interventions.
The ideal candidate will have:

The role requires more than document compilation: the jobholder must interpret client requirements, identify gaps, challenge incomplete information, research and verify supporting technical evidence, and determine the clearest and most persuasive way to communicate Securex solutions. Engineering design and final technical approval remain the responsibility of the designated technical engineers.
Main Responsibilities
Tender Interpretation and Compliance
Review RFQs, RFPs, tender documents and client briefs to understand the required technical scope, deliverables, evaluation criteria and submission instructions.
Develop and maintain compliance matrices, tender checklists, clarification registers and evidence schedules.
Identify omissions, contradictions, assumptions and risks, and coordinate the required clarifications before proposal development proceeds.
Ensure that every technical requirement is answered directly or supported by an accurate cross-reference to the relevant proposal section or appendix.
Technical Proposal Development
Work with solution engineers to convert survey findings, BOQs, system designs and technical notes into clear, persuasive and technically coherent proposals.
Develop the proposal structure, understanding of requirements, solution narrative, and scope of work, methodology, implementation plan, testing and commissioning approach, training plan and support framework.
Standardise equipment descriptions, personnel profiles, project references, statutory evidence and controlled appendices across the submission.
Identify and resolve issues including offline devices, communication failures, power interruptions, inaccurate location reporting, and sensor malfunctions.
Review the complete proposal for consistency between the narrative, BOQ, drawings, compliance statements and manufacturer documentation.
Solution Communication and Visualisation
Determine the clearest way to communicate each solution using system architectures, workflows, equipment profiles, comparison tables, timelines, photographs and visual summaries.
Prepare or coordinate professional diagrams and page layouts that help non-technical evaluators understand how the proposed system will operate.
Apply Securex branding, document hierarchy and formatting consistently while maintaining readability across long and complex submissions.
Manage Word documents containing multiple sections, orientations, tables, images, appendices, headers, footers, cross-references and automatic content fields.
Technical Research and Validation
Research OEM products, part numbers, datasheets, standards, compatibility requirements and available alternatives in support of the engineers’ proposed solution.
Verify technical claims against authoritative manufacturer information and flag unsupported, outdated or conflicting specifications.
Compare products and presentation approaches, and recommend practical improvements without making unapproved engineering decisions.
Maintain current knowledge of electronic security technologies, tender practices and document-production tools.
Coordination and Document Control
Coordinate inputs from Sales, Engineering, Procurement, Projects, HR, Finance, QHSE and OEM partners, with clear owners and deadlines for outstanding information.
Challenge incomplete input constructively, ask focused follow-up questions and escalate unresolved submission risks in good time.
Maintain controlled proposal files, naming conventions, version history, review comments and final submission records.
Conduct final completeness and presentation checks before technical approval and submission.
Support the handover of awarded opportunities by ensuring the project team receives an accurate record of the approved scope, assumptions and commitments.
Continuous Improvement
Develop and improve proposal templates, content libraries, standard methodologies, CV formats, evidence registers and quality-control checklists.
Use AI-assisted research, drafting and document tools responsibly to improve efficiency while independently verifying technical accuracy and confidentiality.
Capture lessons from tender feedback and completed submissions to improve future proposal quality and win readiness.
Key Competencies and Qualifications
Strong analytical and critical-thinking ability, with the confidence to question unclear information, identify gaps and propose better ways of communicating a solution.
Excellent technical writing, editing and information-structuring skills, with the judgement to simplify complex content without changing its technical meaning.
Basic working knowledge of CCTV, access control, fire detection, intrusion detection, intercom, networking, power and integrated electronic security systems.
Ability to interpret BOQs, floor plans, system architectures, site-survey information, product datasheets and basic technical drawings.
Advanced Microsoft Word capability, including styles, sections, page numbering, tables of contents, tables, cross-references, images and appendix management.
Good Microsoft Excel and PowerPoint skills; proficiency in Visio, AutoCAD, Canva, Adobe tools or similar diagram and design applications is an advantage.
Strong visual communication and document-design judgement, with the ability to select the right diagram, table, image or narrative format for the information being presented.
Good product-research and fact-verification skills, including the ability to locate and validate authoritative OEM information.
Creative, curious and resourceful, with the ability to think beyond the information provided while recognising when technical confirmation is required from an engineer.
Strong communication and interpersonal skills, with the confidence to engage engineers, managers, suppliers, tender teams and clients professionally.
Excellent attention to detail, document-control discipline, time management and ability to work accurately under tender deadlines.
Required qualifications/experience
Diploma or degree in ICT, engineering, telecommunications, business information technology, technical communication or a related discipline.
Two or more years of experience in technical proposals, tender documentation, bid coordination, technical pre-sales, electronic security, ICT or an engineering environment is preferred.
Demonstrable experience preparing or coordinating professional technical proposals, tender responses, compliance matrices, BOQs or similar technical documentation.
Exposure to electronic security systems, low-voltage systems, systems integration or related technical solutions is strongly preferred.
Experience working with engineers and converting technical inputs into client-facing documents will be an advantage.
A portfolio or practical assessment demonstrating technical writing, document organisation, visual presentation and problem-solving ability may form part of the selection process.

Seek to inspire others to Christian commitment, faith, and living.
Contribute towards and maintain a positive Christian spiritual environment.
Exhibit characteristics of being a lifelong learner.
Maintain a positive operational environment focused on growth and excellence.
Consistently model professionalism.

will operate, set up, test, maintain and troubleshoot sound and lighting equipment – this requires a strong ear for tone, balance, clarity (overall sound quality) and appropriate lighting techniques.

Job Description
The Chief Operating Officer (COO) is a crosscutting enabling role within the Digital Business Unit (DBU), created to support the Managing Director and the DBU’s functional teams (Commercial, Digital Operations & Service, Technology, Data & AI, Customer Experience, Product, Pricing & Actuarial, and Thrive & Ecosystem) in delivering the unit’s strategic plan. The role provides a unifying layer of Finance, Performance Management, Portfolio Governance and Operating Model leadership that helps functional teams stay resourced, aligned and unblocked to deliver. The COO translates strategy into coordinated execution owning the DBU’s performance framework and operating model effectiveness, governing enterprise portfolio and investment decisions, consolidating financial performance, and providing transformation governance to ensure that the DBU operates profitably, compliantly, and at pace.
KEY TASKS AND RESPONSIBILITIES
Partner with the MD and ExCo in strategic and operational decision-making, translating DBU strategy into coordinated execution across functional teams, and setting KPIs to measure and improve business performance
Own the DBU performance framework – strategic and operational KPIs, benefits realization, and quarterly business reviews – providing the MD and ExCo with a consistent, evidence-based view of business performance
Drive the scaling of the DBU's digital, platform and technology-enabled propositions, directing process improvement, automation, and digital transformation programmes that strengthen competitiveness and delivery efficiency
Own accountability for enterprise portfolio governance across the DBU, including initiative prioritization, resource allocation, investment governance, and delivery decisions
Own DBU operating model effectiveness, including governance structures, organizational effectiveness, and cross-functional alignment across the departments
Provide cross-functional operational governance for the DBU, establishing consistent policies, internal controls, and risk and business continuity standards as well as champion a strong risk and control culture in partnership with functional heads
Own the DBU's Finance function, overseeing budget planning, cost tracking, and financial reporting across all functions, and embedding cost discipline and unit economics thinking into operational and portfolio decisions
Set governance standards for project and portfolio delivery, prioritizing initiatives and surfacing delivery risks and dependencies for MD/ ExCo decision-making as well as and hold functional teams accountable for delivery against agreed actions and timelines
Lead DBU transformation governance, tracking adoption of new tools, ways of working, and process redesign across functions, and reporting on benefits realisation and change roadmap progress to the MD and ExCo
Facilitate structured coordination between the MD, ExCo, and functional heads on finance, portfolio, operations, and transformation matters, and coordinate preparation for management and board meetings by consolidating inputs into a single, evidence-based narrative
Identify cross-functional process and delivery bottlenecks spanning multiple DBU teams, and support engagement with internal and external stakeholders (e.g. regulators, commercial partners, technology vendors) on cross-functional deliverables, in collaboration with functional heads
SKILLS AND COMPENTENCIES
Excellent leadership and management skills to lead cross-functional teams, oversee multiple workstreams, and ensure execution of strategic and operational plans
Strong strategic thinking abilities to provide guidance and insight across a wide range of business and operational matters
Sound commercial and financial acumen, including P&L management, budgeting, and the ability to make informed, data-driven business decisions
Digital and technology fluency, with the ability to engage credibly with engineering, product, and data teams and translate technical concepts into business outcomes
Exceptional organisational skills to manage multiple projects, systems, and timelines concurrently, ensuring objectives are met on time and within budget
Superb interpersonal skills to build positive relationships with staff, stakeholders, partners, and regulators
Top-notch communication skills to convey information effectively across audiences, from operational teams to the board
Effective problem-solving ability to quickly identify and resolve issues that could hinder operational or business performance
Change management and digital transformation experience, with the ability to lead teams through periods of rapid growth and process change
Ability to work under pressure, exhibiting resilience and the capacity to operate in a fast-paced, ever-changing digital business environment
Strong understanding of the insurance industry, including its regulatory environment, challenges, opportunities, and competitive landscape
KNOWLEDGE & EXPERIENCE
Significant experience (10+ years) in senior operations, finance business partnering, PMO/portfolio management, or business management roles, with demonstrable experience consolidating budgets and financial performance across multiple teams or functions
Demonstrated experience scaling digital, platform, fintech or technology-enabled financial services businesses as well as a track record of leading process improvement, automation, or digital transformation programs
Proven experience in planning and budgeting, demonstrating financial acumen and the ability to make informed business decisions
Working knowledge of insurance products, distribution models, and the regulatory environment governing insurance and financial services
Experience leading portfolio governance and leading cross-functional portfolio governance across multiple business areas
Experience supporting executive committees and boards with performance reporting and decision support

Master's degree in Business Administration (MBA) or a related field is preferred

Job Description:
Job Purpose
The Regional Supply Chain Coordinator establishes and maintains end-to-end visibility of the EVD supply pipeline and coordinates the timely mobilization and delivery of critical supplies to the Democratic Republic of the Congo and agreed neighbouring-country locations.
The post holder translates operational requirements into coordinated procurement, supplier-delivery, transport, customs, storage and last-mile plans; identifies bottlenecks and implements or escalates mitigation actions; and provides weekly analysis, projections and status reporting to operational decision-makers and other key stakeholders.
The position supports the establishment and operationalisation of the logistics hub in Uganda and, once the hub is functional, coordinates the import, storage and re-export of EVD items upon authorised request. The role also supports logistics information management, operational reporting and coordination through the Incident Management Support Team and other relevant forums.
Job Duties and Responsibilities
Supply chain pipeline coordination and visibility
Establish, maintain and regularly validate an end-to-end pipeline tracker covering all multilateral supplies, from approved requirement and procurement status through supplier readiness, dispatch, international transport, customs clearance, storage, onward movement and confirmed delivery.
Liaise with bilateral Red Cross and Red Crescent partners and relevant external partners to exchange supply-tracking information and maintain a consolidated operational view while respecting agreed information-sharing protocols.
Maintain forward pipeline projections using operational requirements, consumption rates, available stock, quantities in transit, procurement lead times and expected delivery dates, and identify anticipated gaps or excesses early.
Monitor critical milestones, dependencies and bottlenecks; agree mitigation actions with accountable teams; follow actions through to closure; and promptly escalate delays or risks that could affect continuity of the EVD response.
Operational planning, procurement and supplier delivery
Plan with the EVD operation and the Supply Chain Team in the Democratic Republic of the Congo the procurement, replenishment and delivery of safe and dignified burial kits, body bags, personal protective equipment kits and other approved critical items.
Translate validated operational needs into time-phased supply plans and coordinate with relevant regional and global procurement and supply chain teams so that sourcing and delivery arrangements reflect priorities, lead times, quality requirements and available funding.
Coordinate with suppliers on production and delivery schedules, item readiness, quality and transport documentation, packing and labelling, collection arrangements, dispatch dates and estimated arrival dates; address exceptions and supplier-performance issues without delay.
Assess delivery options, including air, road, sea and multimodal routes, and provide clear recommendations based on urgency, cost, capacity, access, customs constraints and operational risk.
Support timely mobilization and delivery of critical supplies, ensuring that agreed corrective or contingency measures are activated when planned timelines are at risk.
Cross-border movements and Uganda logistics hub
Coordinate the delivery, prepositioning or authorised redistribution of safe and dignified burial kits and body bags with relevant neighbouring-country delegations and National Societies.
Together with the Supply Chain Team in Uganda, support the establishment and operational readiness of the logistics hub, including workflows, roles and responsibilities, import and re-export arrangements, storage controls, inventory visibility, transport interfaces and supporting documentation.
Once the hub is functional, coordinate the import, receipt, storage, order processing and re-export of EVD items against approved requests, ensuring stock accountability and timely dispatch.
Coordinate cross-border movements with clear processes for customs, exemptions, transit documentation, freight forwarding, border handover, transport and last-mile delivery, working with the responsible IFRC and National Society teams in each country.
Ensure that shipment files contain complete and consistent transport, customs, warehouse and proof-of-delivery records, and that shipment status is promptly reflected in the consolidated pipeline.
Job Duties and Responsibilities (continued)
Analysis, reporting and information management
Prepare and share a concise weekly supply chain analysis and pipeline report with key stakeholders, covering stock position, requirements, procurement status, supplier readiness, shipments in transit, projected deliveries, constraints, risks, mitigation actions and decisions required.
Maintain accurate and timely data for agreed supply chain indicators, including order status, lead time, stock coverage, customs dwell time, on-time delivery and unresolved bottlenecks.
Support information-management dashboards, situation reports and operational updates with validated logistics-pipeline data, narrative analysis and forward projections, as applicable.
Ensure that material changes, critical shortages, delayed deliveries and emerging cross-border constraints are communicated outside the regular reporting cycle when operational decisions are required.
Coordination and representation
Ensure timely coordination among logistics and supply chain counterparts at global, regional and country levels, including the IFRC Country Delegation and the Democratic Republic of the Congo Red Cross, as appropriate.
Coordinate with Movement partners, bilateral partners, Emergency Response Units, suppliers, freight and customs service providers, and other operational partners involved in the EVD supply chain.
Represent supply chain in the Incident Management Support Team, relevant supply chain or logistics groups, and appropriate government and external coordination bodies, as delegated by the line manager.
Work closely with Health, Operations, Finance, Procurement, Information Management and other relevant functions to align priorities, confirm decision ownership and maintain realistic delivery plans.
Maintain clear action logs, decision records, contact lists and handover documentation so that pipeline management and partner coordination can continue without disruption at the end of the assignment.
Compliance, quality and risk management
Ensure activities are coordinated in accordance with IFRC supply chain procedures, the applicable delegation of authority, donor conditions, national regulations and relevant quality, safety and documentation requirements.
Identify and monitor risks related to supplier delay, product quality, transport capacity, customs clearance, cross-border restrictions, stock loss, data quality, security and last-mile access, and maintain practical mitigation and contingency measures.
Support due diligence, audit-ready records, segregation of duties and transparent decision-making for transactions and movements coordinated through the position.
Duties applicable to all staff.
Work actively towards the achievement of IFRC’s goals.
Abide by and work in accordance with the Red Cross and Red Crescent principles.
Perform any other work-related duties and responsibilities that may be assigned by the line manager.
Education
University degree in supply chain management, logistics, procurement, business administration, engineering, economics or another relevant field, or an equivalent combination of education and substantial relevant professional experience. Required.
Recognised professional qualification or advanced training in procurement or supply chain management (for example CIPS, CILT or equivalent). Preferred.
Relevant training in emergency response, medical commodities, customs, warehousing, information management or project management.
Preferred.
Experience
At least 5 years of progressively responsible experience in humanitarian supply chain, procurement or logistics, including experience in a coordination role. Required.
Demonstrated experience managing end-to-end supply pipelines and coordinating suppliers, international transport, customs, warehousing and last-mile delivery in an emergency operation. Required.
Experience coordinating across country, regional and global teams and working effectively without direct supervisory authority. Required.

Experience establishing or operationalizing a regional logistics hub or emergency prepositioning facility. Preferred.
Knowledge, Skills and Languages
Strong knowledge of end-to-end humanitarian supply chain management, including procurement, supplier management, transport, customs, warehousing, inventory control and last-mile delivery. Required.
Strong analytical ability and practical skill in developing pipeline trackers, forecasts, lead-time analyses, status reports, risk logs and decision-ready recommendations. Required.
Ability to coordinate multiple stakeholders, clarify accountabilities, negotiate solutions and drive time-critical actions through influence. Required.
Ability to identify operational bottlenecks, evaluate routing and delivery options, and implement proportionate mitigation and contingency measures. Required.
Knowledge of import, export, re-export, transit and customs-clearance processes and the documentation required for cross-border movements. Required.
Sound understanding of supply chain compliance, supplier due diligence, quality assurance, audit trails and segregation of duties. Required.
Advanced user of Microsoft Office, particularly Excel, and practical experience with ERP, shipment-tracking, warehouse or business-intelligence systems. Required.
Ability to work under pressure, manage competing priorities and travel at short notice in accordance with operational and security requirements. Required.
Fluent spoken and written English. Required.

Working knowledge of another language relevant to the response area. Preferred

Job Description:
PURPOSE OF THE ROLE
BBC World Service is creating a new Horn of Africa Language Services Unit in Nairobi, bringing together BBC Somali, BBC Afaan Oromo, BBC Tigrinya and BBC Amharic under a single editorial leadership structure for the first time.
BBC Somali is one of the most trusted international news services for Somali-speaking audiences in Somalia, Ethiopia, Kenya and across a substantial and highly engaged diaspora. It is a service with strong editorial heritage and, under this new structure, significant opportunity: the transformation to a digital-first, video-led operation that can reach a new generation of Somali audiences who consume news primarily through smartphones, YouTube and social media.
BBC Somali is now transforming into a story-led model built around two complementary editorial streams: On the Day and On Demand.
WHY JOIN THE TEAM
The Journalist is the core production resource of both On the Day and On Demand streams. Whether working a morning, afternoon or night shift within On the Day, or contributing to planned video and podcast production within On Demand, the Journalist is expected to move fluently between platforms, formats and roles (such as writing a web article, filming, editing, presenting videos and voicing a radio package and publishing a social post), often on the same story, within the same shift.
This transformation demands journalists who are not simply willing to work across platforms, but who think across platforms instinctively. That means asking, before production begins, how a story will serve audiences on multiple platforms like, the website, on YouTube, on TikTok and on radio and making deliberate choices about format, length and angle for each content.
YOUR KEY RESPONSIBILITIES AND IMPACT:
Write clear, accurate and engaging articles for the BBC Somali website daily, producing content that is well-structured, properly sourced, SEO-aware and published to deadline.
Produce and present short-form video contents including news moments, explainers, interviews and reaction pieces optimised for publication on YouTube, TikTok, Instagram Reels, Facebook and YouTube Shorts, as a standard part of daily output.
Produce and present radio programmes or visualised podcast as needed.
Self-shoot, present and edit short video contents using mobile or camera equipment, applying strong visual judgement, clear audio, appropriate framing and basic graphic or caption overlays to produce content that meets BBC Somali’s production standards.
Contribute to BBC Somali’s visualised podcast and linear radio output, performing on screen as well as on air and understanding the specific demands of presenting and reporting for a simultaneous radio and YouTube streaming audience.
Research, script, film and edit video contents independently or in collaboration with Video Journalists, ensuring content is well-sourced, clearly structured and appropriate for the target platform.
Develop and maintain a range of contacts across Horn of Africa to support original newsgathering, tip-offs and on-the-ground reporting, and use those contacts to contribute stories and angles that go beyond wire and agency copy.
Contribute to live coverage of breaking news events across all platforms including livestreaming, producing timely, accurate content at pace while maintaining BBC editorial standards.
YOUR SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE
ESSENTIAL CRITERIA:
Proven ability to produce content across multiple digital platforms including a news website, YouTube, TikTok, Instagram reels and Facebook and radio with an understanding of the editorial and production requirements of each.
Strong digital writing skills, including the ability to produce clear, accurate, well-structured articles in Somali that are engaging for online readers and appropriately optimised for search.
Experience of producing and presenting short-form video content for social media platforms, including vertical formats for TikTok and Instagram reels, with a clear understanding of what makes short video content hold attention and drive shares. Practical experience of self-shooting video using mobile or camera equipment, with the ability to apply sound visual judgement in a range of settings including studio, location, interview and news-gathering environments.
Confidence presenting to camera, with the ability to deliver scripts, interviews and two-ways clearly and naturally for both broadcast and streaming audiences.
Experience of producing content for radio, including writing scripts for the ear, voicing packages and conducting interviews for broadcast.
Solid experience of sourcing, verifying and reporting news accurately and impartially under deadline pressure, including the ability to apply verification techniques to social media content and user-generated material.
Fluency in written and spoken Somali and English with the ability to write, sub-edit and present in both languages to a high professional standard.
Knowledge about data-driven approach to content development, with experience using audience analytics and platform insights to inform commissioning, optimise performance and grow engagement, particularly among younger and female audiences.

Job Description:

Maintain required security registers, records and documentation for internal review and audit purposes.

Prepare and manage the security department budget within approved limits and ensure efficient use of security resources.
Monitor security equipment, uniforms, communication devices, access-control assets and other operational resources.
Validate security service deployment and supporting records for management review and service-provider performance monitoring.

Submit timely security, incident, risk and contractor-performance reports to management.
Maintain accurate registers for incidents, patrols, visitors, access violations, investigations, security risks and corrective actions.
Analyse security trends and recommend operational improvements to reduce recurring incidents and vulnerabilities.

Work closely with Operations and Site/Factory Management on security requirements and site controls.
Coordinate with HR on people-related matters arising from security incidents and with Loss Control on matters involving loss prevention or operational controls.
Coordinate with ICT on electronic security systems and with HSE on safety, fire and emergency preparednessmatters.
Escalate material security risks, incidents and unresolved control weaknesses through the approved managementstructure.
Qualifications & Experience
Bachelor's degree in Security Management, Criminology, Security Studies, Business Administration or a related field.
Professional certification such as CPP, PSP, CSMP or an equivalent security qualification is an added advantage.
Minimum of 7 years of progressive security experience, including at least 3 years in a managerial/supervisoryrole within a multi-site, manufacturing, logistics, warehousing, commercial or comparable operationalenvironment.
Demonstrated experience in physical security operations, security contractor management, incident investigation, electronic security systems and emergency planning.
Working knowledge of applicable Kenyan security, safety and emergency-response requirements.
Key Competencies
Physical security operations, risk assessment and loss prevention.
CCTV, alarm, access control and security technology management.
Vigilance & Risk Judgement: Strong observation and analytical skills to identify threats, assess risk and make timely operational decisions.
Problem-Solving & Communication: Clear written and verbal communication, sound investigation skills and the ability to coordinate across functions.

Role description
BOMA is seeking qualified and experienced Mentors to deliver day-to-day implementation of the SOIL Program in Marsabit County. This is a field-based role whereby the mentor is responsible for program delivery by providing participants with monthly coaching, mentorship, facilitation, training, linkages to markets and follow-up activities to ensure the effective and quality implementation of the SOIL program towards the achievement of nutrition, livelihoods, entrepreneurship, savings, resilience, and child well-being outcomes. The mentor must be a member of the community/villages where the project is being implemented with clear understanding of the community culture, language and geographical coverage. The will serve as a frontline link between BOMA and participating households and community structures.
Reporting to the Field Officer, the Mentor will take lead in participant mobilization, targeting and enrolment, VSLA group formation and strengthening, capacity building, business coaching, monitoring progress of interventions and data collection. He/she will ensure smooth collaboration with key stakeholder in the community including the government structures relevant for the program deliver outcomes. The mentor delivery the expected roles with adherence to BOMA's program quality, policies, safeguarding, and accountability standards.
Requirements
MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS AND REQUIRED COMPETENCIES
At least a Diploma in Business Administration, Entrepreneurship, Agribusiness, Agriculture, Community Development, Nutrition, Community Health, Public Health, Social Work, Development Studies, Project Management or another relevant field.
At least 2 years of relevant experience in community-based programme implementation, livelihoods, entrepreneurship, nutrition, agriculture, economic inclusion, financial inclusion or resilience programming.
Demonstrated experience in community mobilization, participant mentorship, business coaching or savings group facilitation.
Experience working with women, pastoralist communities or other vulnerable and rural populations is highly desirable.
Experience using digital data collection tools and Microsoft Office is desirable.
Good interpersonal and communication skills.
Good coaching and facilitation skills.
Ability to work independently with minimum supervision.
Motivated, self-driven and accountable.
OTHER REQUIREMENTS
Must be a resident of the respective SOIL program implementation location/village.
Fluency in English and Kiswahili.
Fluency in the relevant local language spoken in the assigned location.
Strong basic computer and digital literacy.
Ability to work in remote and challenging environments.
Must have a Valid motorcycle riding license Class A1/A2. This is mandatory because the mentor is required to ride a motorcycle daily as he/she delivers the program activities in the field.
